- When sentiment is negative or mixed in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 10–15d horizon.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias of 3–7% for 30d forecast.
- If sentiment turns bearish mid-horizon (e.g., -1.00 after +1.00s), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–10% from 15d onward.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00s), especially if recent price is volatile; add 1–3% upward bias for 30d.
- Mean reversion is stronger in sentiment-neutral periods; if 3+ consecutive 0.00s, forecast should be closer to 14d moving average.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common; apply “lag correction” — subtract 1–3% for each day after spike if sentiment remains positive.
